editorial:
Imagine feeling like the black sheep of your family while everyone expects you to have your life together. That is exactly where you find Hashir, Alan, Ajin, and Vinayak. These four buddies are the ultimate troublemakers who have spent their whole lives being called losers by their teachers and parents. The movie captures that awkward, stressful transition into adulthood where you suddenly realize the world does not care about your excuses. It feels like hanging out with a group of chaotic friends who are just trying to figure out where they fit in without losing their minds.

You will love how the chemistry between the four leads feels totally real and not forced. The jokes land well, and the emotional moments hit hard because they feel honest. While the middle part drags a bit, the payoff at the end makes it worth the wait. If you want the best experience, definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the great cinematography, or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you are into collecting physical discs. It is a perfect pick for a movie night with your own group of friends.
endingExplained: The story wraps up with the four friends finally stopping the blame game. After a big confrontation with their families, they realize that being successful does not mean following a set path. They start a small business together that uses their unique skills. The final scene shows them years later, happy and stable, proving to everyone that they were never actually losers, just late bloomers who needed a different kind of support.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about friendship and overcoming failure.
